findings.F1: The tested carry shows only where the profile is really choppy calm, and only at the top of the forecast. On in-profile grid bars (regime "unknown", 7-day non-overlapping), the top z14 quintile (0.95 to 2.88) ends +7.61 % above drift (t 2.73, n 29), while the middle quintiles give +0.93 % and +0.89 % (t 0.45, 0.41). With my own profile rebuild, the choppy-calm slope of the 7-day unusual move on z14>0 is +7.24 % per unit (t 3.66, clustered by day, 39 cases on 18 days). On all folds, though, the slope's t was 1.0 and the unusual move per case was +0.05 %, so the effect is thin and rests on a few days.
findings.F2: The down side of the theme is there too. In-profile, the lowest z14 quintile ends -3.20 % below drift (t -2.22, n 29) and the next -3.51 % (t -1.52). In my choppy-calm rebuild with z14<0, the slope is +13.99 % per unit (t 2.20, 21 cases on 15 days): the larger the swing-scaled fall, the lower the next 7 days.
findings.F3: In agitated markets the same swing-scaled 14-day rise turns against itself. With z14>0, the slope of the 7-day unusual move is -10.90 % per unit in falling agitated (t -2.21, 39 cases, 13 days) and -5.51 % in agitated bars before the 60-day trend is known (t -3.12, 65 cases, 30 days). In rising agitated it is +0.62 % (t 0.20).
findings.F4: A 30-day daily swing that is small against the coin's own 90-day swing is followed by a rise, graded over the lower quintiles. On 7-day grid bars (all profiles), the lowest ratio quintile (0.34 to 0.74) ends +6.62 % above drift (t 3.24, n 65), the next +2.59 % (t 1.40) and the middle -3.35 % (t -2.27); the upper two are -1.58 % and -0.59 %. This t is not clustered by day, and it is one of about a dozen angles I looked at.
findings.F5: Large one-day falls rebound the next day. The lowest decile of the day's return over the 30-day swing gives +0.92 % next day (t 4.26, n 745), and the slope on down days is -0.79 % per unit (t -2.08, 3,599 cases, 808 days). It is strongest in falling agitated (mean +1.14 %, t 2.14). This repeats the agitated and falling-agitated rebound ideas the map already holds, so it is not a discovery.
findings.F6: The book's best and worst days are the market's days. On the top 2 % of days the book makes +2.81 % while the coins rise +7.22 %; on the bottom 2 % it loses -2.82 % against -7.11 %. Window means range from -0.19 %/day (w14) to +0.19 %/day (w17). Days in a position are 18 %, and the unusual move per case (0.05 %) is 0.2 times the 0.22 % trade cost, so the book earns the coins' drift rather than timing.
findings.F7: The other angles did not hold up against the number of looks. Range over swing is U-shaped rather than graded: +0.87 % for the narrowest quintile, -1.40 % (t -3.97) for the second, +1.08 % for the widest. Close location within the day's range showed no quintile with |t| above 1.3. The weekday pattern (Wednesday -0.44 %, t -2.60; Friday +0.37 %, t 2.85) is close to the held late-week idea.

ideas.idea: In a choppy, calm market, a coin whose 14-day return is negative against its own daily swing over the past 30 days keeps falling over the next 7 days, and the larger that swing-scaled fall, the larger the further fall.
ideas.consequence: In a choppy calm market a trader can lean short in proportion to a swing-scaled 14-day fall, the mirror of the long carry.
ideas.name: choppy calm swing fall carries

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, a coin whose 14-day return is positive against its own daily swing over the past 30 days falls back over the next 7 days, and the larger that swing-scaled rise, the larger the fall back.
ideas.consequence: A trader can fade swing-scaled rallies in falling agitated markets, a short box the map holds only twice.
ideas.name: falling agitated rally fades

ideas.idea: A coin whose daily swing over the past 30 days is small against its daily swing over the past 90 days rises over the next 7 days, and the smaller that ratio, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader can lean long on coins whose recent swing has compressed against their quarter's swing, with a move per case far above the 0.22 % cost of a trade.
ideas.name: swing compression precedes rise
